reference_sql:
SELECT subscription_id, user_id, plan_name,
       COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY plan_name) AS plan_starts
FROM subscriptions
WHERE start_date >= DATE '2025-08-01' AND start_date < DATE '2025-09-01'
alternatives:
WITH august AS (  -- one row per subscription that started in August 2025
  SELECT subscription_id, user_id, plan_name
  FROM subscriptions
  WHERE start_date >= DATE '2025-08-01' AND start_date < DATE '2025-09-01'
),
plan_counts AS (  -- one row per plan with August 2025 starts
  SELECT plan_name, COUNT(*) AS n_starts
  FROM august
  GROUP BY plan_name
)
SELECT a.subscription_id, a.user_id, a.plan_name, pc.n_starts AS plan_starts
FROM august a
JOIN plan_counts pc ON pc.plan_name = a.plan_name

SELECT s.subscription_id, s.user_id, s.plan_name,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM subscriptions s2 WHERE s2.plan_name = s.plan_name AND s2.start_date >= DATE '2025-08-01' AND s2.start_date < DATE '2025-09-01') AS plan_starts
FROM subscriptions s
WHERE s.start_date >= DATE '2025-08-01' AND s.start_date < DATE '2025-09-01'

),
plan_counts AS (  -- one row per plan with August 2025 starts
  SELECT plan_name, COUNT(*) AS n_starts
  FROM august
  GROUP BY plan_name
)
SELECT a.subscription_id, a.user_id, a.plan_name, pc.n_starts AS plan_starts
FROM august a
JOIN plan_counts pc ON pc.plan_name = a.plan_name
other_way.tradeoff: Counting each plan in a step of its own and joining back works on any engine, but it takes two steps.
